steps.text: Find parcel-41 in the MessageId column. Write down the two row labels you see.
steps.help: If you marked four rows, you used the subject. Read the last two digits of each message ID.

steps.title: Try the prompt
steps.text: Give the helper the CSV and the prompt, or write its answer yourself offline. Look for a line each for dock and stores.
steps.help: If both statuses are the same, cover the other rows and read the final cell on each of the two matching rows.

steps.title: Challenge the cause

title: Audit a proposed command before trusting it
summary: A suggested change uses a real cmdlet. Check whether it belongs on that side of the route and whether it is even needed.
requires: Download the practice kit and unzip it. Open its cases folder. You can do the checks on paper or in a text editor while offline. Use only the made-up extracts for any AI trial.
features: Trace each cmdlet and parameter to Microsoft Learn. Compare a read-only result with the proposed action.
roles: Read each hybrid connector on the side that owns it.
Check that a command fits the service where it would run.
Stop an export if it found the wrong object.
prompt: Review two suggestions for H1–H4: read the outbound connector on premises; change the cloud connector right away. Name the right session and read-only cmdlet for each side. List the evidence, approval, preview support and rollback note needed before any change.

steps.title: Check the suggestions against the command cards
steps.text: Find Get-OutboundConnector and Get-ReceiveConnector in the sources. Point to the service and the Identity parameter on each page. The first is for Exchange Online. The second is for on-premises Exchange. Offline, use the command facts in the next two steps.
steps.help: A real command name may still be wrong for the chosen session. Leave permission and availability unknown until the actual practice session is checked.

steps.title: Exchange Online PowerShell · outbound read
steps.text: Assume an authorized practice session is already connected. Read this block for H2. On paper, confirm the name and the smart host. If you have an approved matching training object, the block saves exactly one matching cloud connector as CSV.
steps.help: The names here are fictional. Without that training object, use H2 as the supplied output. The checks stop a broad or wrong result. A fresh output path prevents overwriting an old report.
steps.code:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$name = 'RelayToShop'
$rows = @(Get-OutboundConnector -Identity $name -ErrorAction Stop)
if ($rows.Count -ne 1 -or $rows[0].Name -ne $name) { throw 'Unexpected cloud connector.' }
$rows | Select-Object Name,Enabled,UseMXRecord,@{Name='SmartHosts';Expression={$_.SmartHosts -join '|'}} |
    Export-Csv -LiteralPath ./cloud-connector.csv -NoClobber -NoTypeInformation

steps.title: On-premises Exchange Management Shell · receive read
steps.text: Use this separate block in an already-connected on-premises training shell only. From H3 predict the exact identity and Enabled value. The new CSV should describe a single receiving connector.
steps.help: On paper, H3 supplies the identity and state. If the command is missing in a workspace, stop and record the missing access or session detail.
steps.code:
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$id = 'SHOP01\Relay intake'
$rows = @(Get-ReceiveConnector -Identity $id -ErrorAction Stop)
if ($rows.Count -ne 1 -or [string]$rows[0].Identity -ne $id) { throw 'Unexpected site connector.' }
$rows | Select-Object Name,Identity,Enabled |
    Export-Csv -LiteralPath ./site-connector.csv -NoClobber -NoTypeInformation

steps.title: Review a proposed change on paper
steps.text: Look up Set-OutboundConnector and check that SmartHosts and WhatIf are documented together. In an authorized, connected Exchange Online practice shell, this optional read-only check reports whether the installed command exposes those two parameters. Expect two True values if both are available.
steps.help: For an approved change, use -WhatIf only on a cmdlet that supports it. A preview cannot prove delivery. Capture the old value, owner, rollback trigger and retest first. In this exercise, the owner’s recorded action and tests are H6 through H8.

steps.title: Exchange Online PowerShell · optional approved preview
steps.text: For the exercise, read the following block on paper. Only an owner rehearsing this exact change with approval in a matching training session would run it. The final line includes -WhatIf and makes no configuration change. Keep the old target and the rollback condition in the change note.
steps.help: If the name, old host or supported parameters differ, stop. Do not remove -WhatIf. Use H6 through H8 for the fictional change and its delivery tests.

steps.title: Prove a local report can stop safely
steps.text: With PowerShell installed, open a terminal in the kit’s cases folder. Run the supplied command below. Open the CSV. It should have labels S1 and S2. Try the command again with EV-99 and a fresh output name.
steps.help: If PowerShell is unavailable, filter entra-signins.csv by EV-31 on paper. Two rows match. Nothing matches EV-99. The script stops for an unknown event or an existing output path.

check: The cloud read is Get-OutboundConnector -Identity. The on-premises read is Get-ReceiveConnector -Identity.
The Learn syntax for Set-OutboundConnector includes SmartHosts and WhatIf. A dry run does not verify the destination receipt.
The local policy report has two rows for EV-31 and leaves out the account. Unknown events fail before export.

steps.help: C6 gives the stop condition. A passing receipt does not erase a failed control.

steps.title: Return to the recorded evidence
steps.text: Restore the real W4 on your worksheet. Write the verdict with W1, W3 and W4. Ask a second reader to find the same rows.
steps.help: If the conclusion covers every mailbox, narrow it to these two probes. C7 states what you cannot check.

check: The example rollback restores “invioce” and retests both types of mail if the ordinary message is tagged.

features: Read a small evidence packet, name a test and keep a verdict you can defend.
requires: Open the practice files below or in the kit. You can do the whole case on paper offline. An approved AI chat is optional.

title: Capstone: Run one mail case in four tools
summary: Score Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat against the same five facts. Unseal the retest only after scoring.
requires: Use the printed prompt and the answer key in the practice ZIP. Four approved chat tools and internet access are needed for live results. For an offline run, use the paper sample in the packet.
features: Compare first replies against evidence. A result marked unavailable earns no score.
roles: Use a passing delivery to narrow a failed mail trace.
Use the same question and evidence to review an access case.
Grade four bug reports against the same controls.
prompt:
Use only the five rows below. This case is fictional. You have no tenant access.
State the symptom. Compare a sender-wide limit with a limit on one recipient. Cite row IDs. Say what is still unknown. Pick one read-only check to separate the two ideas. Predict what each result would mean. Give no change command.

R1 | 09:02 UTC | dispatch@example.test to workroom@example.test | total message 14 MB | Failed
R2 | 09:04 UTC | same sender to workroom@example.test | total message 1 MB | Delivered
R3 | 09:05 UTC | same sender to stores@example.test | same 14 MB message | Delivered
R4 | 09:02 UTC | delivery error for R1 | message exceeds the size allowed for this recipient
R5 | undated training worksheet | planned receive limit for Workroom: 20 MB

steps.title: Freeze the test first
steps.text: Save the practice ZIP, unzip it and open cases/vendor-trial.txt. Read only the first five rows and the question. You should see one failed large message and two delivered messages.
steps.help: Find R1, R2 and R3. If you saw the later results, keep them out of the messages you send.

steps.title: Collect first replies
steps.text: Start four fresh approved chats. Send Your prompt once to each. Record the tool, date, visible model or “not shown,” and the first reply. Offline, mark the four rows untested and score the paper reply instead.
steps.help: Use the same five rows every time. If one tool is unavailable, leave that row unscored and keep working with the others.

steps.title: Point to the controls
steps.text: Underline the parts of each reply that explain R2 and R3. Check whether it calls R5 a plan. Give a point only when a reply meets the matching item in the key.
steps.help: A pass for small mail tests the recipient. A pass for the same large mail to Stores tests the sender. Giving both points requires both comparisons.

steps.title: Write a useful run note
steps.text: Write the score, one strong piece of evidence and one miss in each finished row. An observation might say “Cited R3 but skipped the live limit check.”
steps.help: If your note only says “best answer,” name the specific row the tool used or missed. Mark an unavailable answer “unscored.”

steps.title: Test the verdict
steps.text: Open V1 through V4. Compare the 14 MB failure before the approved practice change with V3. Compare the larger control with V4. Write down the old limit in case the change must be rolled back.
steps.help: Both results matter. V3 proves the target message passed. V4 shows that the larger message still hit the limit.

check: The packet has one identical first prompt for all four tools. Every scored answer has a saved first reply and a line of evidence.
The hand-written practice answer earns four of five. It asks for a change without first checking the actual receive limit.
